title: MEMORIALS OF WHAT GOD HAS DONE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, took the whole region of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maakathites; it was named after him, so that to this day Bashan is called Havvoth Jair.) And I gave Gilead to Makir. But to the Reubenites and the Gadites I gave the territory extending from Gilead down to the Arnon Gorge (the middle of the gorge being the border) and out to the Jabbok River, which is the border of the Ammonites. - Deut 3:14-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses continues detailing the boundaries and the names given to the conquered regions — Jair naming an area after himself, Gilead given to Makir, the Reubenites and Gadites receiving their territories. These place names and boundaries became lasting markers of what God had done. "To this day Bashan is called Havvoth Jair," Moses notes, showing how the memory was preserved in the very names of the land.

Names have a way of preserving memory. Long after the events, the names on the map would remind people of how God had given this land to His people. Every time someone spoke the name "Havvoth Jair," they were, in a small way, recalling the story of God's provision. The geography itself became a testimony.

This reminds us of the value of markers and memorials in our own walk with God. Throughout Scripture, God's people set up stones, gave names, and marked places to remember His works. When Samuel set up a stone, he named it "Ebenezer," saying, "Thus far the Lord has helped us" (1 Sam 7:12). These markers helped God's people remember and give thanks.

We can create our own "markers" of God's faithfulness — journals, dates we remember, ways of recalling how God has helped us "thus far." These serve the same purpose: keeping God's works before our eyes so we do not forget. And the greatest marker of all is the cross, the eternal testimony of God's love and faithfulness in Christ. As we remember what God has done, from the small mercies to the great salvation in Jesus, our hearts are filled with gratitude and our faith is strengthened for whatever lies ahead.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What "markers" help you remember God's faithfulness in your life?
2. How might creating memorials of God's help strengthen your gratitude?
3. How does the cross stand as the greatest marker of God's faithfulness?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me to mark and remember Your faithfulness, saying with grateful heart, "Thus far the Lord has helped me." Keep Your works before my eyes, above all the cross, that testimony of Your love in Christ. Amen.
